# hivelocity_dns_record_a (Resource)

Manages an A record set in a Hivelocity-hosted zone. The API addresses A records by zone name and record name rather than by numeric ID, and a record name can carry several addresses (round robin). The resource ID is `<domain>/<name>`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "hivelocity_dns_domain" "example" {
  name = "example.com"
}

resource "hivelocity_dns_record_a" "www" {
  domain    = hivelocity_dns_domain.example.name
  name      = "www"
  addresses = ["66.165.231.122", "66.165.231.123"]
  ttl       = 3600
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `addresses` (Set of String) IPv4 addresses the record resolves to.
- `domain` (String) Zone name the record belongs to, for example `example.com`.
- `name` (String) Record name, for example `www` or `@` for the zone apex.
- `ttl` (Number) Time to live of the record, in seconds.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import with <domain>/<record name>
terraform import hivelocity_dns_record_a.www example.com/www
```
